cover.headline: IKEA makes you build it. {Then you love it more.}
cover.credit: Photo: Raysonho / CC0 via Wikimedia Commons

slides.label: TRICK #1
slides.headline: The path is {one-way.}
slides.body: Most IKEA stores wind you past room after room before you reach the warehouse. You can't see what's ahead, so you *keep walking.* Ingka's head of retail says shoppers get reminded of things they *"talked about three weeks ago, but forgot."*

slides.label: THE TEST
rows: IKEA opens its *first store* in Älmhult, Sweden.
IKEA tried *choose-your-path* layouts in some cities.
Stores in *Madrid, Shanghai and Warsaw* were shut. Shoppers wanted to be guided.

slides.label: TRICK #2
slides.headline: Then you {build it} yourself.
slides.body: Psychologists Michael Norton, Daniel Mochon and Dan Ariely ran a *2012* study. People who assembled an IKEA box were willing to *pay significantly more* for it than people who just bought one built by someone else.

slides.label: THE CATCH
slides.headline: It only works if you {finish.}
slides.body: In the same research, the effect *disappeared* when people failed to complete the task, or built something and then saw it destroyed. ==Effort creates love, but only with a win.==

last.headline: Make customers {work a little,} and they value it more.
last.body: But only if they can finish what they started. Would you rather buy it built or build it yourself?
